Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+y}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,{∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,
$$

which of the following could be the definition of the rectangular domain $R?$

I. $R=[-1,3]\times [-2,1]$

II. $R=[-1,2]\times [-2,2]$

III. $R=[-2,3]\times [-2,2]$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+y}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given rectangles.

- Rectangles I and II do not cover the region $D.$

- Rectangle III covers the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
